newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police accused of brutality in Guerrero.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police accused of brutality in Guerrero.

text.p: Leftist legislators in the troubled Mexican state of Guerrero accused local police Wednesday of torture and kidnapping in raids on two villages earlier this month.

State police illegally arrested eight people, beat others including women and children and illegally searched homes on Feb. 15 in the municipalities of Tlacoachistlahuaca and Xochistlahuaca, Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) federal deputy Eliseo Moyao told reporters after a fact-finding trip.

He said the group of about 100 police were responding to shots fired at a police vehicle the day before in the region, which killed one policeman. Police accused the villagers, who are Mixtec Indians, of carrying out the attack, he added.
PRD legislators said that of the seven adults and one child arrested without warrants or evidence, only four were in prison and that the other four, including a 12-year-old boy, had disappeared.
No comment was immediately available from Guerrero state authorities.

Although it is home to the world-famous tourist resort of Acapulco, Guerrero is also one of Mexico's poorest, most violent states. The Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a Marxist guerrilla group, operates there as well as armed drugs gangs and bands of highway robbers.
